chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who was unaware that he had to perform the obligatory tawaf of the House. He said: If that was due to ignorance in the hajj, he must repeat it, and a camel is due from him.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Kazim or al-Rida عليه السلام, addressed by this kunyah in the narration
key_terms.أَعَادَ: he must repeat or redo the required rite
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: the Sacred House, meaning the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْجَهَالَةِ: ignorance or lack of knowledge of the ruling
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: a camel offered as sacrificial compensation
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory circumambulation required in hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone ignorantly leaves the obligatory tawaf in hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who failed to perform the obligatory tawaf of the Ka'bah out of ignorance during hajj. The Imam عليه السلام states that he must repeat the hajj act and that a badanah is also required, showing the seriousness of neglecting this essential rite even when done in ignorance.
